# Project Intake Form (Existing System)

## Metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project | prototype_19 (codename `p19`; crates `p19-client`, `p19-server`, `p19-shared`) |
| Repository | `github.com/nchashch/p19` (branch `main`; 232 commits, last 2026-10-09) |
| Intake type | Existing system (brownfield), generated by `intake-from-codebase` |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0001–0019, bug_0001–0011, playtests 0001–0051 (index), `docs/agents/skills/*`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, crates.io (2026-10-28) |
| Source state | commit `184371f` (2026-10-09) |
| Date | 2026-10-28 |
| Owner | Nikita Chashchinskii |

This page summarises; `AGENTS.md` (current state) and the ADRs (why) are authoritative.

## System Overview

A Bevy 0.19 3D multiplayer game prototype built "always multiplayer": even singleplayer runs a local client and server. A headless authoritative server (`p19-server`: levels from `.glb` with Avian colliders, players, movement, combat, spawning) and a client (`p19-client`: rendering, UI on bevy_markup, input, camera, VR) agree through `p19-shared` (replication registration, messages, bundles, states). Networking is lightyear 0.30 over UDP/netcode with per-client tokens over TLS; movement is server-authoritative with optional client prediction through bevy_ahoy. Steam Deck is the minimum-spec target. The studio's agent-playtesting method started here (ADRs 0009–0012; 51 playtest reports), and bevy_mcp_harness was extracted from it.

## Problem and Outcomes

- Prove an always-multiplayer architecture (authoritative server, prediction, rollback, interest management) on Bevy.
- Develop it with agents that playtest the real game headlessly and file bugs and reports.
- Run on Steam Deck with identical content across hardware.

## Current Scope and Features

| Feature | State | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Connect → lobby → pick a level → play (movement, combat, spawning) | built, end to end from a fresh clone with Git LFS | `AGENTS.md` |
| Room-based interest management (game / lobby rooms and roots) | built | ADR 0003 |
| Character separate from the connection entity | built | ADR 0004 |
| bevy_ahoy KCC over replicated BEI input; optional client prediction | built | ADR 0008, 0017 |
| Server determinism hardening and session record/replay | built; replayed movement mismatches live | ADR 0013, `AGENTS.md` Known gaps |
| Per-client netcode tokens over TOFU-pinned TLS; portable builds | built (dev-grade) | ADR 0014 |
| Client UI on bevy_markup (HTML/CSS/Fluent), system fonts | built | ADR 0015, 0016 |
| Agent tool API (BRP/MCP via bevy_mcp_harness), `--mcp` and `--no-render` clients | built | ADR 0009–0012 |
| VR (OpenXR) | built, not re-verified on a headset | `AGENTS.md` Known gaps |
| Disconnect cleanup, per-player spawn points, level switching, NPC input path, character authoring pipeline | missing | `AGENTS.md` Known gaps |

## Architecture (Current State)

Cargo workspace with three members; the server is headless and authoritative, the client sends intent and renders replicated state. Details: @AGENTS.md ("Architecture: client / shared / server", "Dependency layout").

## Scale and Performance (Current)

A few clients per server in playtests; Steam Deck (~4 GB VRAM) is the budget, met with KTX2/BC6H assets. No load testing.

## Security and Compliance (Current)

- Netcode tokens issued over TLS with a self-signed, TOFU-pinned certificate: dev-grade; production needs a CA-signed certificate on a real backend.
- The agent tool API is behind the `dev-tools` feature, localhost only.
- Code MIT OR Apache-2.0; original assets CC0 (ADR 0018).

## Team and Operations (Current)

One developer with AI agents (omp with GLM, opencode, Claude Code). ADRs, bug reports, playtest reports per run. CI builds the server and a shippable steamrt4 client; it runs no tests. Commits go straight to `main`.

## Dependencies and Infrastructure

| Dependency | Use |
|---|---|
| Bevy 0.19.1 | engine |
| lightyear 0.30, avian3d 0.7, bevy_ahoy 0.2, bevy_enhanced_input 0.26 | netcode, physics, character controller, input |
| bevy_markup 0.4.0, bevy_mcp_harness 0.3.1 | UI, agent tool API (studio crates) |
| bevy_hanabi, bevy_seedling, bevy_mod_outline (fork), bevy_skein, bevy_asset_loader, bevy_common_assets, bevy_mod_openxr/xr/xr_utils | VFX, audio, outlines, Blender authoring, assets, VR |
| gltf fork (`KHR_texture_basisu`), fluent-syntax fork | `[patch.crates-io]` |
| Git LFS | binary assets |

## Known Issues and Technical Debt

From `AGENTS.md` "Known gaps": disconnected players never cleaned up; all players spawn at one point; no level switching; the only level renders black; no NPC input path; replay movement mismatch; no ground friction; VR grip poses likely untracked; dev-grade netcode; dead code and five unused dependencies; a handful of unit tests. The studio's other repositories are on Bevy 0.20; this one is a version behind (@.aiwg/planning/bevy-0.20-migration.md).

## Why This Intake Now?

Fifth member of the studio's AIWG workspace (root `../aiwg`): a requirements baseline, risk register, test strategy and a Bevy 0.20 migration plan derived from the repository's records.

`AGENTS.md` has no next-steps section; its Known gaps are the backlog. The Bevy 0.20 migration waits on its blockers (the plan).

<!-- aiwg-managed -->
<!-- Generated structure by AIWG; operator content is protected by markers. -->

## AIWG Context Graph

This file is the canonical provider-neutral home for project and operator context.
Provider startup files are generated adapters: they direct the harness here first,
then to AIWG.md for framework discovery and routing.

### Precedence

1. Platform capability and safety constraints are absolute: what a harness can do, what it is
   permitted to do, and its refusal boundaries. Nothing here overrides those.
2. AIWG rules deployed to this project bind over any provider, harness, or session *directive*
   on a subject an AIWG rule covers — including a directive that claims to supersede earlier
   guidance. A harness decides how a tool is invoked; it does not set project policy.
3. Root WORKSPACE.md supplies shared project/operator context.
4. AIWG.md supplies generated framework/discovery context.
5. Narrower linked files and provider-native subtree instructions govern their declared scope,
   within the ceiling set above.

The distinction in 1 vs 2 is capability versus preference. "This tool is unavailable" is a
constraint. "Format commits this way" is a directive, and an AIWG rule on commit content wins.
When a directive and an AIWG rule conflict, follow the rule and say plainly that you did.

### Ownership

- Edit project-neutral notes only inside the protected Project Context section below.
- Keep detailed policies, runbooks, hooks, and quickrefs in linked files.
- `.aiwg/context/providers/` is reference only: no provider bootstrap auto-loads it.
  Put directives you want read into Project Context above.
- Never store secrets, tokens, credentials, or machine-local sensitive values here.

### Artifact Routing

- Before any agent or provider writes AIWG payload, run `aiwg artifacts path --json --check-write` and write beneath its `artifact_root`.
- Treat `.aiwg/...` in skills and templates as a logical artifact path, not necessarily a repository-local filesystem path.
- Only `AIWG.md`, `aiwg.config`, and `frameworks/registry.json` belong in the repository-local `.aiwg` control plane.
- If the configured external artifact root is unavailable, stop with an actionable error; never fall back to repository-local payload.

- [Project-local quickref](.aiwg/quickref.json) (when configured)

`docs/agents/adr/`, defects in `docs/agents/bug_reports/`, agent playtest runs in
`docs/agents/playtests/`, procedures in `docs/agents/skills/`. **`docs/humans/` is human-only:

the agent docs (index: `.aiwg/index.md`; the Bevy 0.20 migration plan in `.aiwg/planning/`); keep
them current in the same change.

This repository is a member of the `noetic-basho-technologies` AIWG workspace (root: `../aiwg`).

ADR 0019 (the follow-up ADR 0007 named).

Solution Profile (Current System)

# Solution Profile (Current System)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0001–0019, bug ledger, playtest index, CI workflow |
| Source state | `184371f`, 2026-10-28 |

## Current Profile

**Pre-release prototype with a production-shaped architecture.** The networking model (authoritative server, prediction, rollback, interest management, tokens over TLS) and the agent QA practice (51 playtests, 11 bugs all fixed) are well beyond prototype norms; automated testing is not (7 unit tests, CI builds only). Idle since 2026-10-09 and a Bevy version behind the rest of the studio.

| Dimension | Level | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Security | Dev-grade | TOFU-pinned self-signed TLS for tokens (`AGENTS.md`) |
| Reliability | Medium | known gaps: no disconnect cleanup, single spawn point, no level switching |
| Testing & quality | Low automated, high exploratory | 7 unit tests; 51 agent playtests; no gameplay tests in CI |
| Process rigor | High | 19 ADRs, bug and playtest skills, AGENTS.md as current state |

## Recommended Profile Adjustments

- Turn the most-used playtest flows (connect, lobby, move, attack) into a scripted headless smoke run in CI, through the agent tool API (R-003).
- Remove the five unused dependencies before the Bevy 0.20 migration (the plan).

## Improvement Roadmap

1. Disconnect cleanup and per-player spawn points (the most visible gaps).
2. Bevy 0.20 migration when its blockers clear (@.aiwg/planning/bevy-0.20-migration.md).
3. A CA-signed token endpoint before any public build.

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0014-multiplayer-hardening-netcode-tokens-and-portable-builds.md
- @docs/agents/bug_reports/README.md
- @docs/agents/playtests/index.md

Test Strategy

# Test Strategy

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `test/test-strategy-template.md` (condensed) |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("Known gaps", "Commands", "Agent tool API and headless modes"), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, playtest index, `docs/agents/skills/playtest.md` |
| Source state | `184371f`, 2026-10-28 |

## Context and Objectives

Quality here comes from agents playtesting the real game: a server plus headless clients driven over the agent tool API, each run filed as a playtest report (51 so far) and each defect as a bug report (11, all fixed). Automated tests are few by circumstance, not design (`AGENTS.md` Known gaps).

## Test Levels and Scope

| Level | What | Where | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | player name generation (4), token server-address fallback (3) | `p19_shared::player`, `p19_server::networking` | `cargo test --workspace` (not in CI) |
| Build | server; shippable steamrt4 client | CI | every push |
| Agent playtest | connect, lobby, levels, movement, combat, UI, options; screenshots and UI dumps | `--mcp` / `--no-render` clients over BRP/MCP; `docs/agents/playtests/` | per change |
| Replay | deterministic server replay of recorded sessions | `server --replay` | on demand (movement mismatch open) |
| Platform | Steam Deck build and run | steamrt4 toolbox | by hand |

**In scope:** the three crates. **Out of scope:** dependencies (forks tracked in `AGENTS.md`).

## Automation Strategy

CI builds only. The first step is a scripted headless smoke run in CI (risk R-003), then the migration's regression check (@.aiwg/planning/bevy-0.20-migration.md).

## Defect Management

Bug reports in `docs/agents/bug_reports/` per `docs/agents/skills/bugreport.md`; playtest reports per `docs/agents/skills/playtest.md`, newest first in `docs/agents/playtests/index.md`. Index: @.aiwg/testing/defect-register.md.

## Requirements and Risk Coverage

Most requirements in @.aiwg/requirements/supplementary-spec.md are covered by playtests only; automated: NFR-SEC-001 (token address), NFR-SUP-003 (names), NFR-PLAT-003 (steamrt4 build).

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/playtests/index.md
- @docs/agents/skills/playtest.md
- @docs/agents/skills/bugreport.md

## Context and Objectives

Quality here comes from agents playtesting the real game: a server plus headless clients driven over the agent tool API, each run filed as a playtest report (51 so far) and each defect as a bug report (11, all fixed). Automated tests are few by circumstance, not design (`AGENTS.md` Known gaps).

## Test Levels and Scope

| Level | What | Where | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | player name generation (4), token server-address fallback (3) | `p19_shared::player`, `p19_server::networking` | `cargo test --workspace` (not in CI) |
| Build | server; shippable steamrt4 client | CI | every push |
| Agent playtest | connect, lobby, levels, movement, combat, UI, options; screenshots and UI dumps | `--mcp` / `--no-render` clients over BRP/MCP; `docs/agents/playtests/` | per change |
| Replay | deterministic server replay of recorded sessions | `server --replay` | on demand (movement mismatch open) |
| Platform | Steam Deck build and run | steamrt4 toolbox | by hand |

**In scope:** the three crates. **Out of scope:** dependencies (forks tracked in `AGENTS.md`).

# AIWG.md
<!-- aiwg-managed -->
<!-- CLAUDE.md companion for non-Claude providers. -->

CLAUDE.md was not found at project root. AIWG.md normally mirrors that content.
See [.aiwg/AIWG.md](.aiwg/AIWG.md) for the project framework context.

<!-- AIWG-PARALLELISM-CAP:START -->
## Parallelism Cap

This project caps parallel agent fan-out (#1359):

- **max_parallel_subagents**: 4 (provider default for claude)
- **max_parallel_ralph_loops**: 2 (provider default for claude)
- **max_parallel_mc_missions**: 4 (provider default for claude)

*Rationale*: Provider default for claude — adjust via 'aiwg config set --project parallelism.max_parallel_subagents N'

### Model-selected delegation rubric

For each non-trivial task, assess whether it contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. When delegation is supported, prefer the deployed model-pinned wrappers by task characteristics and consequence:

- `aiwg-model-efficiency-worker`: discovery, inventory, focused edits, and other bounded low-cost work.
- `aiwg-model-coding-worker`: implementation, tests, debugging, and routine technical delivery.
- `aiwg-model-reasoning-worker`: architecture, synthesis, difficult analysis, and high-consequence review.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly coupled changes, serial dependencies, or tasks likely to collide in shared state; also keep work local when coordination costs exceed the expected benefit. Parallelize only independent work, and take the MIN of provider limits, `max_parallel_subagents`, `AIWG_CONTEXT_WINDOW` budget, framework-specific caps (including the RLM 7-agent hard cap for RLM dispatches), and natural task decomposition. Bump the project cap via `aiwg config set --project parallelism.max_parallel_subagents N`.

The primary agent retains orchestration, final integration, conflict resolution, validation, and user-facing accountability.

**Provider behavior (claude)**: native custom subagents can select the deployed model-worker wrapper. Verify the resolved model when provider or account policy may substitute it.

<!-- AIWG-PARALLELISM-CAP:END -->

<!-- aiwg-context-finalization:START -->
## Context Finalization

This section is synthesized after template emission from the current workspace state. Preserve operator-authored content outside AIWG-managed blocks; rerun `aiwg regenerate` to refresh this section after provider, framework, or MCP wiring changes.

### Workspace Snapshot

- Configured providers: claude
- Installed frameworks/addons: all
- Recorded deployments: claude
- Normalized project context: `.aiwg/AIWG.md`

### Discover-First Protocol

Classify every user turn FIRST: is it a **new directive** or a continuation? When a message names or references an AIWG command/capability — even as pasted content like an `address-issues` tracker table, an issue list, or a `flow-*` name — treat it as a new directive and ACT: run `aiwg discover "<the need>"`, fetch with `aiwg show <type> <name>`, and invoke it. Do NOT ask "what would you like me to do with these?" when the action is implied — a pasted `address-issues #1234` table means run the address-issues workflow on those issues.

Also run `aiwg discover` before declining an AIWG request as out of scope or inventing a workflow from memory. The CLI ranks AIWG capabilities across the installed corpus and rebuilds the index from `$AIWG_ROOT` automatically, so a "no matches" for a command you know is deployed is a bug — not a signal it is absent. Commands AIWG deploys to your provider command directory (`.opencode/command/`, `.claude/commands/`, `~/.codex/prompts/`, …) ARE discoverable this way; fetch them with `aiwg show command <name>`. This prevents decline-without-search failures, ask-instead-of-act on new directives, and hallucinated skill or agent names. Full rule: `agentic/code/addons/aiwg-utils/rules/skill-discovery.md`.

### Engagement Verification

When a user asks whether AIWG is active or engaged in this project, run or read `aiwg status --probe --json` and report the result plainly: engaged state, project root, deployed provider files, installed frameworks/addons, and the next action from the probe. Do not add AIWG attribution, signatures, generated-by text, or passive footers to user files, commits, PRs, comments, code headers, or docs.

### Tracker Authority Protocol

- Source of truth: [.aiwg/aiwg.config](./.aiwg/aiwg.config)
- Internal/canonical tracker: `origin` (github; git@github.com:nchashch/p19.git)
- Customer issue tracker: not configured
- Primary repo remote: `origin`; CI remote: `origin`
- Secondary/mirror remotes: none configured
- Issue storage mode: not configured

Tracker access order for issue, PR, release, and CI-sensitive tracker operations:
1. MCP/app tools for the configured tracker.
2. Tracker HTTP API with configured credentials.
3. Tracker CLI for the configured tracker, after confirming authentication.
4. Stop and report a blocker.

- Project config decides tracker authority; installed/authenticated CLIs do not.
- Route internal engineering, delivery, and CI-sensitive issue work to the internal tracker.
- Route customer acknowledgements, follow-up, and closure to the customer tracker when configured.
- Git SSH remote access is repository sync, not issue-tracker API access.
- Do not file on mirror or secondary remotes just because their CLI is authenticated.
- Treat an unauthenticated tracker CLI as one failed access path, then continue probing MCP/app/API before blocking.

### Source Model

- `.aiwg/AIWG.md` is the normalized project-local context entry point.
- Root `AIWG.md` is the generated cross-provider companion loaded through `AGENTS.md` and provider twins.
- `AGENTS.md`, `WARP.md`, `.hermes.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` are provider-facing bridges, not replacements for `.aiwg/AIWG.md`.
<!-- aiwg-context-finalization:END -->

## Parallelism Cap

This project caps parallel agent fan-out (#1359):

- **max_parallel_subagents**: 4 (provider default for claude)
- **max_parallel_ralph_loops**: 2 (provider default for claude)
- **max_parallel_mc_missions**: 4 (provider default for claude)

*Rationale*: Provider default for claude — adjust via 'aiwg config set --project parallelism.max_parallel_subagents N'

### Model-selected delegation rubric

For each non-trivial task, assess whether it contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. When delegation is supported, prefer the deployed model-pinned wrappers by task characteristics and consequence:

- `aiwg-model-efficiency-worker`: discovery, inventory, focused edits, and other bounded low-cost work.
- `aiwg-model-coding-worker`: implementation, tests, debugging, and routine technical delivery.
- `aiwg-model-reasoning-worker`: architecture, synthesis, difficult analysis, and high-consequence review.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly coupled changes, serial dependencies, or tasks likely to collide in shared state; also keep work local when coordination costs exceed the expected benefit. Parallelize only independent work, and take the MIN of provider limits, `max_parallel_subagents`, `AIWG_CONTEXT_WINDOW` budget, framework-specific caps (including the RLM 7-agent hard cap for RLM dispatches), and natural task decomposition. Bump the project cap via `aiwg config set --project parallelism.max_parallel_subagents N`.

The primary agent retains orchestration, final integration, conflict resolution, validation, and user-facing accountability.

**Provider behavior (claude)**: native custom subagents can select the deployed model-worker wrapper. Verify the resolved model when provider or account policy may substitute it.

Chain of Custody Log

# Chain of Custody Log

> This document records the collection, transfer, and storage of all evidence for the referenced case.
> Every person who handles evidence MUST log a transfer entry. Gaps in custody chain may compromise
> the admissibility of evidence. Complete all fields — do not leave entries blank.

---

## Case Information

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Case ID | `{{case_id}}` |
| Case Title | `{{case_title}}` |
| Target System | `{{hostname}}` |
| Investigation Date | `{{investigation_date}}` |
| Lead Investigator | `{{investigator_name}}` |
| Authorized By | `{{authorized_by}}` |
| Authorization Reference | `{{authorization_ref}}` |
| Classification | `{{classification}}` |
| This Document Version | `{{doc_version}}` |
| Last Updated | `{{last_updated}}` |

---

## Evidence Item Register

Each distinct piece of evidence collected during this investigation. Assign a unique ID (E-001, E-002, etc.) to each item at time of collection. Never reuse IDs within a case.

| ID | Description | Source Path / Location | Collection Date/Time | Hash Algorithm | Hash Value | Collected By | Integrity Verified |
|----|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|---------------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| E-001 | `{{evidence_desc_1}}` | `{{source_path_1}}` | `{{collection_datetime_1}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_1}}` | `{{collector_1}}` | `{{verified_1}}` |
| E-002 | `{{evidence_desc_2}}` | `{{source_path_2}}` | `{{collection_datetime_2}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_2}}` | `{{collector_2}}` | `{{verified_2}}` |
| E-003 | `{{evidence_desc_3}}` | `{{source_path_3}}` | `{{collection_datetime_3}}` | SHA-256 | `{{hash_3}}` | `{{collector_3}}` | `{{verified_3}}` |

### Collection Notes

```
{{collection_notes}}
```

### Packet Evidence Bundle Entries (optional)

Add one row when a validated `PacketEvidenceBundle` enters the case. This is an
additive register; existing evidence rows remain valid.

| Evidence ID | Bundle ID | Capture SHA-256 | Bundle Status | TShark Path / Version | Analysis Context / Filter Digest | Received UTC / From / By | Storage | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-XXX | `packet-evidence:...` | `sha256:...` | completed / partial / empty | `/absolute/tshark` / `x.y.z` | `sha256:...` / `sha256:...` | `...` | `...` | `...` |

Keep the full command argv, config digests, derived-artifact hashes, and stable
frame/stream locators in the machine-readable manifest entry. Raw payload stays
withheld unless an explicit case policy permits it.

### Evidence Inventory Commands Used

```bash
# Hash all files in evidence directory at collection time
find /evidence/{{case_id}} -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > /evidence/{{case_id}}/evidence_hashes.sha256

# Verify hashes later (run to confirm no tampering)
sha256sum -c /evidence/{{case_id}}/evidence_hashes.sha256
```

---

## Custody Transfer Log

Record every transfer of evidence between individuals or storage locations. A transfer occurs any time evidence moves from one person's control, or from one storage location, to another.

| Transfer ID | Date / Time | From (Name / Location) | To (Name / Location) | Purpose | Evidence Items | Signature / Confirmation |
|-------------|-------------|----------------------|---------------------|---------|---------------|-------------------------|
| T-001 | `{{transfer_datetime_1}}` | `{{from_1}}` | `{{to_1}}` | `{{purpose_1}}` | `{{items_1}}` | `{{signature_1}}` |
| T-002 | `{{transfer_datetime_2}}` | `{{from_2}}` | `{{to_2}}` | `{{purpose_2}}` | `{{items_2}}` | `{{signature_2}}` |
| T-003 | `{{transfer_datetime_3}}` | `{{from_3}}` | `{{to_3}}` | `{{purpose_3}}` | `{{items_3}}` | `{{signature_3}}` |

**Transfer Protocol:**

- Confirm hash values match before and after any transfer involving digital media
- Both parties must acknowledge the transfer in writing (or via tracked ticketing system)
- Physical media transfers require secure packaging and a transport manifest
- Remote transfers (e.g., SCP, SFTP) must use encrypted channels; log source and destination IPs

---

## Evidence Integrity Verification

Re-run the survey (crates.io `max_stable_version` and its `bevy` requirement per dependency) before starting. ## Dependency survey (2026-10-28) | Crate | In use? | Now | Bevy 0.20 | Upstream state | |---|---|---|---|---| | bevy_ahoy | yes (14 files; the KCC, ADR 0008) | 0.2.0 | **no** | default branch still 0.19, last push 2026-08-06 | | bevy_seedling | yes (4 files; audio) | 0.8.0 | **no** | default branch still 0.19, last push 2026-08-09 | | bevy_hanabi | yes (3 files; VFX) | 0.19.0 | unreleased | "Migrate to Bevy 0.20 and WESL shaders" (#576) merged 2026-10-15; a git dependency works until a release | | bevy_mod_outline | yes (2 files) | 0.13.0, owner's fork `fix/skinned-motion-outline` | **no** | upstream idle since 2026-07-09; the fork needs migrating itself | | bevy_mod_openxr, bevy_mod_xr, bevy_xr_utils | yes (VR) | 0.6.0 | **no** | "Update to bevy 0.20 + openxrs 0.22" (bevy_oxr #212) open | | lightyear (+ `lightyear_avian3d`, `lightyear_inputs_bei`) | yes | 0.30 | 0.31.0 | released 2026-10-21; review its changelog (netcode, inputs) | | avian3d | yes | 0.7.0 | 0.8.0 | released 2026-10-20 | | bevy_enhanced_input | yes | 0.26.0 | 0.27.2 | released | | bevy_skein | yes | 0.6.0 | 0.7.0 | released; Skein-authored `.glb`s may need re-export (reflected type paths) | | bevy_asset_loader, bevy_common_assets | yes | 0.27 / 0.17 | 0.28.1 / 0.18.0 | released | | noiz | yes | 0.5.0 | 0.6.0 | released | | bevy_markup | yes (every UI surface) | 0.4.0 | 0.7.0 (+ unreleased) | studio crate; 4 breaking changes in 0.5–0.7 (form submit, `RemSize`, Markdown interpolation, `` sizing) plus Bevy 0.20 | | bevy_mcp_harness | yes (`dev-tools`) | 0.3.1 | 0.4.0 | studio crate; `physics_debug` removed in 0.4.0 — avian3d 0.8 now supports 0.20, so the harness can restore it | | vleue_navigator | **no** (0 references) | 0.16 | 0.17.0 | remove | | bevy_simple_text_input | **no** | 0.15.0 | no | remove | | bevy_vrm1 | **no** | 0.9.5 | studio fork has a `bevy-0.20` branch | remove | | bevy_vello | **no** | 0.14.0 | no | remove | | audionimbus | **no** (direct only; `bevy_seedling` doesn't use it) | 0.16.0 | no | confirm, then remove | | bevy-steamworks | **no** (declared for Steam integration) | 0.17.0 | no | remove until Steam integration starts | ## Plan **Phase 0 — now, on Bevy 0.19 (no regret).** 1. Remove the six unused dependencies above, and `Character`'s duplicate replication registration and the other dead code `AGENTS.md` lists. Fewer crates to wait for. 2. bevy_mcp_harness: restore `physics_debug` on avian3d 0.8 and release (the client enables `bevy_mcp_harness/physics_debug`). 3. A scripted headless smoke run (server + `--no-render` client: connect, lobby, pick a level, move, attack) through the agent tool API, so the migration has a regression check beyond playtests (R-003). **Phase 1 — start when bevy_ahoy and bevy_seedling release for Bevy 0.20** (the two hard blockers; or decide to migrate them on owner forks, as with bevy_mod_outline and bevy_vrm1). 1. Bevy 0.19.1 → 0.20 and the released crates together: lightyear 0.31, avian3d 0.8, bevy_enhanced_input 0.27, bevy_skein 0.7, bevy_asset_loader 0.28, bevy_common_assets 0.18, noiz 0.6. 2. bevy_hanabi from git (`main`, after #576) until a release. 3. Migrate the bevy_mod_outline fork (the `fix/skinned-motion-outline` patch on top of a 0.20 port). 4. bevy_markup 0.4 → 0.7: the four breaking changes, then a UI playtest of every screen. 5. bevy_mcp_harness 0.3.1 → 0.4 (+ `physics_debug`). 6. VR: if bevy_oxr #212 hasn't landed, feature-gate VR off for the migration rather than wait. 7. Re-export Skein-authored `.glb`s if reflected type paths changed; check the gltf fork (`KHR_texture_basisu`) against 0.20's gltf version. **Verification:** the Phase 0 smoke run, then a full agent playtest (connect → lobby → level → movement with and without prediction → combat → spawning, two clients), a Steam Deck build in steamrt4, and `AGENTS.md` updated in the same change. Record the migration in an ADR (bevy_markup's 0.5.0 and vtuber's ADR 0002 are the studio's previous 0.20 migrations). ## Sources - @AGENTS.md - @docs/agents/adr/0008-adopt-bevy-ahoy-character-controller.md - @docs/agents/adr/0015-client-ui-on-bevy-markup.md - @docs/agents/skills/playtest.md

Use-Case Briefs

# Use-Case Briefs

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `requirements/use-case-brief-template.md` (one brief per section) |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md` ("What this is", "Known gaps", "Commands", "Agent tool API and headless modes"), ADRs 0003–0017 |
| Source state | `184371f`, 2026-10-28 |

Status: **Built** or **Planned**. IDs are stable.

## Actors

| Actor | Who |
|---|---|
| Player | Plays on desktop, Steam Deck or in VR |
| Host | Runs `p19-server` (UDP 6000, token endpoint HTTPS 6001) |
| Agent | AI agent playtesting through the agent tool API (`--mcp` / `--no-render` clients) |
| Developer | Debugs a recorded session with `server --replay` |

## Built

### UC-001 — Player joins a game

- **Main success scenario:** the client fetches a per-client netcode token over TLS (TOFU-pinned), connects over UDP, lands in the lobby room, picks a level; the server loads it and moves the player's character into the game room.
- **Notes:** a disconnected player's character is never cleaned up; a rejoining client then never gets control. Sources: ADR 0003, 0004, 0014, `AGENTS.md` Known gaps.

### UC-002 — Player moves

- **Main success scenario:** BEI actions replicate to the server; bevy_ahoy's KCC moves the character authoritatively; with prediction on, the client runs the KCC too and lightyear rolls back on corrections; look is client-owned absolute input.
- **Notes:** no ground friction; join bursts can delay inputs for ~10 ticks. Sources: ADR 0008, 0017, bug_0004, bug_0009–0011.

### UC-003 — Player fights and spawns objects

- **Main success scenario:** the client sends attack/kill attempts and spawn requests; the server resolves them and replicates the results within rooms.
- **Sources:** bug_0001–0003, `AGENTS.md`.

### UC-004 — Player uses the menus

- **Main success scenario:** main menu, lobby, pause and options screens in bevy_markup (HTML/CSS/Fluent, system fonts, gamepad-first navigation, Steam Deck glyphs).
- **Sources:** ADR 0001, 0015, 0016, playtests 0050–0051.

### UC-005 — Player plays in VR

- **Main success scenario:** with `vr = true` in the client config, OpenXR drives the camera; VR locomotion mocks the movement action.
- **Notes:** grip poses likely never track (bevy_xr_utils 0.6.0); not re-verified on a headset. Source: `AGENTS.md` Known gaps.

### UC-006 — Agent playtests the game

- **Main success scenario:** the agent launches the server and a `--mcp` (offscreen) or `--no-render` client, drives it over BRP/MCP (state, UI tree, screenshots, device-level input, p19's `game/select`/`game/trigger`/`game/levels`), and files a playtest report and bug reports.
- **Sources:** ADR 0009–0012, `docs/agents/skills/playtest.md`, 51 playtest reports.

### UC-007 — Developer replays a session

- **Main success scenario:** the server records a session; `server --replay` re-runs it deterministically.
- **Notes:** replayed movement covers far less distance than live. Source: ADR 0013.

## Planned (from Known gaps)

### UC-101 — Disconnected players are cleaned up

- **Status:** missing; characters persist (`Lifetime::Persistent`).

### UC-102 — Players spawn apart

- **Status:** missing; one spawn point.

### UC-103 — Switch levels without a restart

- **Status:** missing; the server never unloads a level.

### UC-104 — NPCs act through an input path

- **Status:** missing; `Fire<A>` injection is the likely path.

### UC-105 — Character authoring pipeline

- **Status:** designed, mostly unimplemented (`AGENTS.md`).

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0003-room-based-interest-management.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0004-decouple-player-character-from-connection-entity.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0008-adopt-bevy-ahoy-character-controller.md

- @docs/agents/adr/0015-client-ui-on-bevy-markup.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0017-client-owned-absolute-look-input.md
- @docs/agents/skills/playtest.md

# AIWG.md
<!-- aiwg-managed -->
<!-- Normalized project-local AIWG context. Operator notes may live outside AIWG-managed blocks. -->

This file is the stable `.aiwg/AIWG.md` entry point for AIWG skills, rules, and generated provider context.

<!-- aiwg-context-finalization:START -->
## Context Finalization

This section is synthesized after template emission from the current workspace state. Preserve operator-authored content outside AIWG-managed blocks; rerun `aiwg regenerate` to refresh this section after provider, framework, or MCP wiring changes.

### Workspace Snapshot

- Configured providers: claude
- Installed frameworks/addons: all
- Recorded deployments: claude
- Normalized project context: `.aiwg/AIWG.md`

### Discover-First Protocol

Classify every user turn FIRST: is it a **new directive** or a continuation? When a message names or references an AIWG command/capability — even as pasted content like an `address-issues` tracker table, an issue list, or a `flow-*` name — treat it as a new directive and ACT: run `aiwg discover "<the need>"`, fetch with `aiwg show <type> <name>`, and invoke it. Do NOT ask "what would you like me to do with these?" when the action is implied — a pasted `address-issues #1234` table means run the address-issues workflow on those issues.

Also run `aiwg discover` before declining an AIWG request as out of scope or inventing a workflow from memory. The CLI ranks AIWG capabilities across the installed corpus and rebuilds the index from `$AIWG_ROOT` automatically, so a "no matches" for a command you know is deployed is a bug — not a signal it is absent. Commands AIWG deploys to your provider command directory (`.opencode/command/`, `.claude/commands/`, `~/.codex/prompts/`, …) ARE discoverable this way; fetch them with `aiwg show command <name>`. This prevents decline-without-search failures, ask-instead-of-act on new directives, and hallucinated skill or agent names. Full rule: `agentic/code/addons/aiwg-utils/rules/skill-discovery.md`.

### Engagement Verification

When a user asks whether AIWG is active or engaged in this project, run or read `aiwg status --probe --json` and report the result plainly: engaged state, project root, deployed provider files, installed frameworks/addons, and the next action from the probe. Do not add AIWG attribution, signatures, generated-by text, or passive footers to user files, commits, PRs, comments, code headers, or docs.

### Tracker Authority Protocol

- Source of truth: [.aiwg/aiwg.config](./aiwg.config)
- Internal/canonical tracker: `origin` (github; git@github.com:nchashch/p19.git)
- Customer issue tracker: not configured
- Primary repo remote: `origin`; CI remote: `origin`
- Secondary/mirror remotes: none configured
- Issue storage mode: not configured

Tracker access order for issue, PR, release, and CI-sensitive tracker operations:
1. MCP/app tools for the configured tracker.
2. Tracker HTTP API with configured credentials.
3. Tracker CLI for the configured tracker, after confirming authentication.
4. Stop and report a blocker.

- Project config decides tracker authority; installed/authenticated CLIs do not.
- Route internal engineering, delivery, and CI-sensitive issue work to the internal tracker.
- Route customer acknowledgements, follow-up, and closure to the customer tracker when configured.
- Git SSH remote access is repository sync, not issue-tracker API access.
- Do not file on mirror or secondary remotes just because their CLI is authenticated.
- Treat an unauthenticated tracker CLI as one failed access path, then continue probing MCP/app/API before blocking.

### Source Model

- `.aiwg/AIWG.md` is the normalized project-local context entry point.
- Root `AIWG.md` is the generated cross-provider companion loaded through `AGENTS.md` and provider twins.
- `AGENTS.md`, `WARP.md`, `.hermes.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` are provider-facing bridges, not replacements for `.aiwg/AIWG.md`.
<!-- aiwg-context-finalization:END -->

Option Matrix (Project Context and Priorities)

# Option Matrix (Project Context and Priorities)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0003, 0008, 0009, 0013, 0014 |
| Source state | `184371f`, 2026-10-28 |

## Project Reality

- A prototype: the codename stays internal and branding is undecided (`AGENTS.md`).
- The proving ground for the studio's crates (bevy_markup, bevy_mcp_harness) and its agent-playtesting method.
- Product direction elsewhere in the studio: single-player titles with verified leaderboards (infrastructure ADR 0011, 0016); this prototype stays multiplayer.

## Priorities (weights sum to 10)

| Priority | Weight | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Correct, authoritative multiplayer (server decides; prediction optional) | 3 | ADR 0003, 0004, 0008, 0017 |
| Agent-driven QA on the real game | 3 | ADR 0009–0012, 51 playtests |
| Steam Deck as min-spec, identical content across hardware | 2 | `AGENTS.md` Platform targets |
| Post-release debuggability (determinism, replay) | 2 | ADR 0013 |

## Trade-offs Already Made

- bevy_ahoy's KCC over a custom controller (ADR 0008); prediction off by default.
- System fonts over bundled CJK fonts (ADR 0016 superseding 0002).
- Join-burst input corrections accepted, not fixed (`AGENTS.md`).

# SDLC Index — prototype_19

_Generated: 2026-10-28 — 10 pages · consumer `sdlc-complete` · workspace `noetic-basho-technologies` (root: `../aiwg`)_

Derived pages cite their sources with `@path` mentions; provenance records are in `.aiwg/research/provenance/records/`. Authoritative: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/adr/`, `docs/agents/bug_reports/`, `docs/agents/playtests/`, `docs/agents/skills/`. `docs/humans/` is human-only.

## Intake (3)
- [Project intake](intake/project-intake.md) — always-multiplayer Bevy 0.19 prototype: authoritative server, prediction, rooms, tokens over TLS; agent playtesting's origin
- [Solution profile](intake/solution-profile.md) — production-shaped architecture, strong agent QA, few automated tests
- [Option matrix](intake/option-matrix.md) — priorities: authoritative multiplayer, agent QA, Steam Deck, replay

## Requirements (2)
- [Use-case briefs](requirements/use-cases.md) — UC-001–007 built (join, move, fight, menus, VR, agent playtest, replay); UC-101–105 planned (Known gaps)
- [Supplementary specification](requirements/supplementary-spec.md) — multiplayer correctness, security, platform, supportability requirements with their checks

## Risks (1)
- [Risk list](risks/risk-list.md) — R-001–009; highest: a Bevy version behind, no disconnect cleanup, no gameplay tests, one black level

## Testing (2)
- [Test strategy](testing/test-strategy.md) — 7 unit tests, CI builds, 51 agent playtests
- [Defect register](testing/defect-register.md) — bug_0001–0011, all fixed; open gaps in `AGENTS.md`

## Planning (1)
- [Bevy 0.20 migration](planning/bevy-0.20-migration.md) — waiting on bevy_ahoy and bevy_seedling; six unused dependencies to remove now

## Architecture (1)
- [Architecture](architecture/README.md) — pointer to `AGENTS.md` and ADRs 0001–0019

Risk List

# Risk List

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Template | `management/risk-list-template.md` |
| Derived from | `AGENTS.md`, ADRs 0008, 0013, 0014, bug ledger, the dependency survey (2026-10-28) |
| Source state | `184371f`, 2026-10-28 |
| Owner | Project owner (all risks) |

Scales High / Medium / Low; Exposure = Impact × Likelihood. Never renumber.

## Register

| Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Exposure | Mitigation Strategy | Owner | Status | Residual Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-001 | A Bevy version behind the studio: the studio's crates move on 0.20 (bevy_markup 0.4 → 0.7 has 4 breaking changes; bevy_mcp_harness 0.3.1 → 0.4) and the gap grows; the character controller (bevy_ahoy) and audio (bevy_seedling) have no 0.20 release. | High | High | HxH=High | The migration plan: remove unused dependencies now; migrate when the blockers release, or fork them. | Owner | Open | Medium |
| R-002 | Disconnected players are never cleaned up; a rejoining client never gets control until a server restart. | High | High | HxH=High | Clean up on disconnect (non-persistent `ControlledBy` lifetime or an explicit despawn). | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-003 | No gameplay tests: 7 unit tests, CI builds only; regressions surface only in agent playtests. | Medium | High | MxH=High | A scripted headless smoke run through the agent tool API in CI. | Owner | Open | Medium |
| R-004 | Netcode tokens use a TOFU-pinned self-signed certificate: unfit for a public build. | High | Low | HxL=Medium | CA-signed certificate on a real backend before any public release (ADR 0014). | Owner | Accepted | Low |
| R-005 | Session replay doesn't reproduce movement (~1 vs ~12.7 units over 60 ticks), so post-release debugging (ADR 0013) can mislead. | Medium | Medium | MxM=Medium | Fix the injected `Fire<A>` timestamps (the leading suspect). | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-006 | Owner forks to maintain: bevy_mod_outline (skinned-motion fix), gltf (`KHR_texture_basisu`), fluent-syntax; each Bevy bump means rebasing them. | Medium | Medium | MxM=Medium | Upstream the patches; track in `AGENTS.md` "Dependency layout". | Owner | Open | Medium |
| R-007 | VR is unverified: grip poses likely never track (bevy_xr_utils 0.6.0); VR crates have no 0.20 release. | Low | High | LxH=Medium | Re-verify on a headset; feature-gate VR during the migration. | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-008 | Only one level, and it renders black (no lights); no level switching. | Medium | High | MxH=High | Lights in `minimal.level.ron`; level unloading on the server. | Owner | Open | Low |
| R-009 | Repository on the personal `nchashch` account; the studio's other repositories are on `noeticbasho`. | Medium | Low | MxL=Low | Transfer when convenient. | Owner | Open | Low |

## Sources

- @AGENTS.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0008-adopt-bevy-ahoy-character-controller.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0013-server-determinism-and-session-replay.md
- @docs/agents/adr/0014-multiplayer-hardening-netcode-tokens-and-portable-builds.md
- @.aiwg/planning/bevy-0.20-migration.md
